The try block retrieves a constructor that fits the parent and path arguments, then invokes it. If any of the three checked exceptions (InstantiationException, InvocationTargetException, IllegalAccessException) occur during this reflective operation, the catch block catches them and throws a new FactoryException with the original message and cause. The programmer likely chose to throw a runtime exception to avoid forcing all callers to handle these specific checked exceptions, but by using a custom exception type FactoryException, they provide a way for callers to catch and handle factory creation failures if needed.
